title: The Role of Influencers and Echo Chambers in the Diffusion of Vaccine Misinformation: Opinion Mining in a Taiwanese Online Community
screen_reason: Content analysis of 5,818 vaccine-keyword threads from the PTT 'Gossiping' board (Taiwan), hand-coded by two trained coders into true-information and misinformation types, with the verbatim share 1,601 (27.5%) containing misinformation. Meets the CONTENT criterion.

estimates.measure_type: % of vaccine-related threads on Taiwan's PTT Gossiping board coded as containing misinformation
estimates.denominator: 5,818 threads ('boards') containing the Chinese keyword for 'vaccine', scraped from all threads posted on the PTT Gossiping board between January 2021 and December 2022
estimates.definition: A thread counted in the numerator if coded into any misinformation label of the scheme: misleading information (false or inaccurate information, regardless of intention), disinformation (deliberately created and shared with intent to mislead), propaganda (biased or misleading information used to promote a political cause), fabricated content (entirely false content designed to deceive), conspiracy (a secret plot by a group or organization) or mixed misinformation.
estimates.misinfo_def: "In this study, we use 'misinformation' as an umbrella term to encompass all false or inaccurate information disseminated through social media."
estimates.source_quote: Of 5818 threads, 3830 (65.8%) were identified as true information, and 1601 (27.5%) contained misinformation, yielding 5431 boards for analysis.
estimates.page_loc: Abstract, Results; Results, 'Identified Misinformation' and Table 2 (p. 6)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two trained coders working in Mandarin classified an initial sample of 500 posts independently with an inductively developed codebook; Cohen's kappa = 0.91; discrepancies resolved by discussion and, where needed, by the principal investigator. The remaining 5,318 boards were split into two sets (n=2,659 each) and independently coded. A consolidated library of Taiwanese COVID-19 vaccine misinformation from three fact-checking organisations (MyGoPen, Cofacts, Taiwan FactCheck Center) was used as the 'final check' when coders disagreed - so fact-checks entered only as a tiebreaker, not as the primary ground truth.
estimates.moderator_quote: The data for this study were collected from the "Gossiping" board on PTT using a web scraper developed in Python to extract HTML data. The scraping targeted posts made between January 2021 and December 2022. We filtered the dataset using the Chinese term for "vaccine" to ensure we captured vaccine-related threads. ... In total, 5818 boards were pulled.
estimates.notes: 1601/5818 = 27.52%, matching the verbatim 27.5%. INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY THE ADJUDICATOR SHOULD SEE: the misinformation subtype counts in Table 2 sum to 1,810, not 1,601 (misleading 452 + disinformation 97 + propaganda 858 + fabricated 195 + conspiracy 179 + mixed 29 = 1,810; 1,810/5,818 = 31.1%). The 1,810 figure is the one that makes the whole table add up (3,830 true + 1,810 misinformation + 23 religious + 155 unrelated = 5,818 exactly), so the headline 1,601 (27.5%) is arithmetically unexplained; the paper says only that mixed threads were 'recategorized' into conspiracy, which does not change the total. I kept the authors' stated 27.5% as the value, per R8, and flag the discrepancy. BORDERLINE flagged because 'propaganda' - 'biased or misleading information used to promote a political cause or push a certain point of view' - is the single largest misinformation label (858 threads) and a factually TRUE but partisan post could receive it, so the numerator is not purely falsity. Year set to 2021, the start of a two-year (Jan 2021-Dec 2022) collection window. platform_norm=other: PTT is a Taiwanese terminal-based BBS, described by the authors as Taiwan's 'Reddit' but not the Reddit platform.

estimates.measure_type: % of the analysed vaccine threads (unrelated and religious threads removed) coded as containing misinformation - narrower denominator
estimates.value_raw: 1601 misinformation threads of the 5431 boards retained for analysis = 29.5%
estimates.denominator: 5,431 boards retained for analysis (3,830 true + 1,601 misinformation), i.e. the 5,818 scraped threads after excluding 155 unrelated and 23 purely religious threads
estimates.definition: Same numerator as the primary row, expressed over the analysis set the authors carried into the diffusion models rather than over all scraped threads.
estimates.misinfo_def: "In this study, we use 'misinformation' as an umbrella term to encompass all false or inaccurate information disseminated through social media."
estimates.source_quote: After disregarding the unrelated and religious threads, and recategorizing the “mixed ” threads into the conspiracy category, there were 3830 true threads and 1601 threads containing misinformation, for a total of 5431 boards for analysis moving forward.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: As for the primary row (two coders, kappa 0.91, fact-check library as tiebreaker).
estimates.moderator_quote: Posts unrelated to vaccines or involving purely religious content were excluded from the final analysis.
estimates.notes: DERIVED, NOT STATED: 29.5% is not printed by the authors; it is the exact part/whole share of two verbatim counts with the same denominator (1,601 of 5,431 = 29.48%), which R8 permits. Kept only because the choice between the raw keyword corpus (5,818) and the analysis set (5,431) moves the estimate by two points and is exactly the denominator decision the review codes. Drop this row if only author-stated values are wanted.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (1) the per-type shares of the 5,818 threads (misleading information 452, 7.8%; disinformation 97, 1.7%; propaganda 858, 14.7%; fabricated content 195, 3.4%; conspiracy 179, 3.1%; mixed 29, 0.5%) - verbatim subtype breakdowns of the same corpus; I made no rows for them because they are mutually exclusive components of the umbrella row rather than alternative definitions of it, and their sum (1,810) contradicts the stated total (1,601), so any one of them would inherit that inconsistency. An adjudicator who wants a strict-falsity variant could use fabricated content 3.4% or disinformation 1.7%. (2) true-information shares (3,830, 65.8%; factual news 1,603, 27.6%; scientifically accurate analytical content 2,227, 38.3%) and the residual categories (religious 23, 0.4%; unrelated 155, 2.7%) - not misinformation. (3) 'among threads identified containing true information, 608 (15.9%) were shared at least once. Conversely, 165 (10.3%) of misinformative threads were reposted' - the denominator is misinformation threads and the numerator is whether they were reposted, so this is diffusion OF misinformation, not a share of shares that are misinformation; it is not a SHARING content_share and I did not code it. (4) Mean comments/reposts per thread (Table 3: true 74.01 comments / 0.40 reposts; misinformation 52.63 / 0.20) and the negative binomial relative risks (propaganda RR=2.07; disinformation RR=0.48; polarity RR=0.22) - diffusion statistics, not prevalence. (5) Network figures - 23,004 unique users with average volume-polarity 3.27; core network 6,035 users, average polarity 8.70; the effect of removing the top 5%/10% of influential nodes on average polarity (Figure 2) - I considered and REJECTED a CONCENTRATION row: the paper never states a top-X%-of-users-account-for-Y%-of-exposure/sharing pair, only that removing top-centrality nodes lowers an average polarity score, so R1 (both conc_group_pct and conc_share_pct required) is not met.

rob.design: Observational content analysis plus network analysis of secondary, publicly available forum data. Sampling frame: a Python web scraper collected all threads posted on PTT's 'Gossiping' board (the most active board; ~56,000 users/day platform-wide) from January 2021 to December 2022, then filtered on the Chinese keyword for 'vaccine', yielding 5,818 threads; all data in Mandarin Chinese; other boards deliberately excluded. Coding procedure: two trained coders, inductive codebook piloted on 500 posts, Cohen's kappa = 0.91, disagreements resolved by discussion with the principal investigator adjudicating, remaining 5,318 boards split into two independently coded halves, with a library of vaccine misinformation from MyGoPen, Cofacts and the Taiwan FactCheck Center as the reference of last resort. Analysis: threads collapsed to true/false; a 'core network' of users with >=5 posts (robustness-checked over cutoffs 1-10); negative binomial regression of diffusion breadth (n=2,422) with word count and user activeness as controls. No response rate applicable; no ethics approval required (public data). Weaknesses: single board of a single forum; the misinformation subtype counts do not reconcile with the reported misinformation total; diffusion depth unmeasurable by construction of PTT.
